Their total is zero and the first moment equals minus the weighted covariance, with the component along n equal to minus the height variance.

For the binary case the two weights are 1/2, giving the coefficient (h₊−h₋)/4. Against a smooth compactly supported test, distributional divergence of the segment vector measure integrates minus the derivative along the segment, yielding the endpoint difference with the displayed sign.

For the horizontal second divergence, the two cross terms in ∇²_x(hf) contract to zero since the measure is symmetric with An=0. The second derivative of h is zero. This verifies the equality on tests without differentiating the matrix measure pointwise.

For the active support pair the adjusted endpoint values differ by h_{K₊}(n)−h_{K₋}(n)−n·B(p₊−p₋). Distinct bases make the two endpoint Diracs distinct. If every normal is active, equality of the adjusted supports identifies translates. Conversely any translation vector can be prescribed as B(p₊−p₋). The homothetic example has exact Minkowski support equality but nonzero width for the endpoint support difference.
